claims.claim: ⚠️ **Discuss every child with VWD and bleeding with the paediatric haematology team**; plan treatment with a haematologist **before any procedure**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **VWD is the most common inherited bleeding disorder**, affecting males and females equally: easy bruising, mucosal bleeding (epistaxis, oral mucosa, menorrhagia) and post-operative bleeding.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Type 1 (common):** reduced VWF, mild bleeding. **Type 2 (uncommon):** abnormal VWF, variable bleeding. **Type 3 (rare):** near-absent VWF — may bleed like moderate–severe haemophilia, into joints and muscles.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Give clotting factor at once for head injury, major haemorrhage or any suspected internal bleeding**, without waiting for a full assessment to be completed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Establish** the site and extent of bleeding, the VWD type and severity, and any home treatment (e.g. tranexamic acid).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Routine coagulation studies are not required.** Consider FBE and ferritin after recurrent mucosal bleeding — anaemia and iron deficiency are common.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tranexamic acid both treats epistaxis and mouth bleeds and stops them recurring, whatever the VWD severity**, alone or with desmopressin or factor concentrate; often helpful for heavy menstrual bleeding.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dose: oral tranexamic acid, 25 mg/kg per dose up to a maximum of 1.5 g, three times a day for 5–10 days**, according to severity.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Desmopressin is for mild–moderate Type 1 VWD with a documented safe and satisfactory desmopressin challenge.** Occasionally effective in Type 2, **never in Type 3**, and **not adequate alone for major bleeding.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Generally not used under 3 years or with seizure disorders** — it can cause hyponatraemia and seizures. **Fluid-restrict to about 2/3 of maintenance for 24 hours afterwards.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dose: desmopressin 0.3 microgram/kg (max 20 micrograms) once, IV or subcut.** IV: dilute to 50 mL with 0.9% sodium chloride and infuse over at least 30 minutes. Subcut: press on the site for 1–2 minutes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Give clotting factor replacement immediately for severe or life-threatening bleeding.** Biostate (plasma-derived VWF/FVIII) may be needed in Type 1 with severe bleeding or DDAVP failure, and treats bleeding in Types 2 and 3. **Recombinant FVIII contains no VWF.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Prescribe Biostate in Factor VIII units**, rounded to the closest vial size.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Biostate dose by bleed:** oral mucosa/epistaxis/menorrhagia 25 FVIII units/kg (60 VWF units/kg) · GI bleed 40 FVIII units/kg (96 VWF units/kg) · joint/muscle 40 FVIII units/kg (96 VWF units/kg).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **CNS bleed, trauma or surgery: Biostate 60 FVIII units/kg (144 VWF units/kg).**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No aspirin or NSAIDs** (e.g. ibuprofen, naproxen, diclofenac) — they may worsen bleeding.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider transfer for:** suspected intracranial haemorrhage · neck or throat bleeding · forearm or calf bleed risking compartment syndrome · hip or inguinal bleeding (iliopsoas risk) · undiagnosed abdominal pain · persistent haematuria · severe pain · **ongoing mucosal bleeding.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** there is no active bleeding, follow-up is arranged and the family has a management plan (e.g. Haemophilia Treatment Centre Card).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'von Willebrand disease' (Last Updated April 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/von_Willebrand_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23
